headline: Bitget sets dated withdrawal restart from Sept 28; BTC flat $83.9k, 10y at 5.17%
summary: As of 06:22 UTC on 26 September the tape is quiet and slightly heavy: BTC is $83,917.40 against an $84,090.50 open (-0.21%), sitting 36% up its $83,163.60-$85,247.40 daily band, ETH is $2,687.40 (-0.15%) and still the laggard at 27% of a $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range, and SOL is $120.42 (-1.39%), the only one really moving, 2.0% off its $122.91 high but still 3.9% above the $115.85 low and 65% up its range; weekly changes are +3.7% BTC, +2.7% ETH, +7.4% SOL. The one acute crypto wound now has a timetable: Bitget published a staged withdrawal restart at 03:55 UTC today, BTC from 28 September 08:00 UTC, ETH the 29th, USDT the 30th and everything else 2 October, with the $387.5m loss stated as covered by a User Protection Fund that held over $464m. Macro, not crypto, is still setting the range - the US 10-year closed Friday at 5.17% after a 23bp three-session selloff to its highest since June 2007, CME-implied odds of a 25bp October Fed hike are around 73%, and WTI eased 2.3% to about $92.44 on Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal that has produced talks but no deal. The institutional bid is intact but thinning: spot BTC ETFs took $134m on 25 September for a seventh straight day of inflows, 81% below Monday's $999m 2026 high, while Strategy spent $174.0m on repurchasing its own STRC preferred versus $75.7m on bitcoin in the 14-20 September week. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite reads 62.6, both Greed, on 145 items in 24 hours, with Hyperliquid funding mild (0.00060%/h BTC, 0.00125%/h ETH and SOL), BTC futures at a -0.040% discount to spot and SOL open interest down 9% to $683.8m - a de-levered, range-bound weekend book with no dip trigger on the board.

BTC.note: $83,917.40, down 0.21% on the session and 36% up an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band on $3.16bn of open interest, funding of 0.00060%/h and a -0.040% futures discount to spot - range consolidation with no crowded long, not a dip.

ETH.note: $2,687.40, off 0.15% and the weakest of the three at 27% of a $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range and only +2.7% on the week, on $2.97bn of open interest and a flat 0.000% premium, so there is neither pressure nor an obvious bid here.

SOL.note: $120.42, down 1.39% and 2.0% off its $122.91 high after CoinDesk reported at 05:00 UTC that Alpenglow has no firm mainnet date, but still 3.9% above the $115.85 low, 65% up its range and +7.4% on the week, with open interest down 9% to $683.8m - positioning is unwinding, the price is not yet dipping.

drivers.title: Bitget publishes dated staged withdrawal restart, BTC from 28 Sept 08:00 UTC
drivers.detail: Bitget met its deadline, posting a schedule at 03:55 UTC on 26 September: Bitcoin withdrawals resume 28 September at 08:00 UTC, ETH (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism) on the 29th, USDT (Ethereum, BSC, Solana, TRON) on the 30th, and other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October, with CEO Gracy Chen holding an AMA at 07:30 UTC on the 28th. The exchange puts the loss at $387.5m, up from $351.6m after $35.9m of Zcash and TRON transfers were traced, says user balances are unaffected and that the hit sits inside a User Protection Fund that held more than $464m, and has added a 5% bounty on frozen or recovered funds; cold storage was untouched and trading and deposits never stopped.

drivers.title: 10-year at 5.17% after a 23bp selloff; October hike odds near 73%
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield finished Friday 25 September at 5.17% and the 2-year at 4.81%, after a three-session selloff pushed the benchmark up 23bp to about 5.20%, its highest since June 2007. CME FedWatch puts a 25bp hike at the 27-28 October FOMC near 73%, with Polymarket around 64%, and the cited drivers are hawkish Fed commentary, a hot inflation reading, strong data and the absence of concrete progress in the US-Iran talks.

drivers.title: ETF inflows persist but 81% off the week's peak; Strategy buys its own preferred over BTC
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs drew $134m on 25 September, a seventh consecutive inflow day, with IBIT +$96.99m and FBTC +$49.32m against BITB -$11.84m - but that is 81% below Monday's $999m, the largest single day of 2026, so the pace is decaying even as the streak holds. Separately, Strategy's 8-K disclosures show that in the 14-20 September week it put $174.0m of USD Cash into repurchasing its own STRC preferred stock versus $75.7m into bitcoin, and paid $57.4m of preferred dividends and interest, leaving the USD Reserve at $5.04bn and USD Cash at $1.05bn.

drivers.title: Solana's Alpenglow has no firm mainnet date after all
drivers.detail: CoinDesk reported at 05:00 UTC on 26 September that Alpenglow is now live on both devnet and testnet, but that no firm mainnet launch date has been announced: Anza's software schedule only tentatively allows feature activations to resume from 28 September and does not identify that date as the launch. The 150ms finality figure is a simulation target, not a live-network result. That removes the dated catalyst SOL had been carrying into next week, and SOL open interest has already fallen 9% to $683.8m.

drivers.title: Iran's seven-day Hormuz timeline knocks WTI to about $92.44, still no deal
drivers.detail: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi set out a step-by-step timeline on Friday under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen on the sixth day if Washington accepts Tehran's proposal, with US and Iranian negotiators exploring a phased passage-for-blockade-relief swap on the UN General Assembly sidelines. WTI fell 2.29% to about $92.44 and Brent eased to roughly $104.50, but nothing is signed - a similar 17 June memorandum collapsed into renewed fighting, and the bond desk is explicitly citing the lack of concrete progress as an inflation risk.

drivers.title: US crypto policy keeps thinning: Peirce out 2 Oct, CLARITY stalled, Kalshi loses again
drivers.detail: Hester Peirce, who ran the SEC's Crypto Task Force, leaves on 2 October, cutting the agency to Chair Atkins and Mark Uyeda, and the former CFTC leader running the Blockchain Association is departing after the Senate's CLARITY Act cloture vote failed. A second appeals court also ruled against Kalshi, holding that sports prediction contracts are subject to state regulation, while the Federal Reserve has opened public comment on two proposals for supervising payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

watch.what: Bitget CEO Gracy Chen's AMA, thirty minutes before BTC withdrawals are due to reopen at 08:00 UTC. The schedule is dated but withdrawals stay frozen for two more days, so this is where the story either closes cleanly or slips a second time - the timetable already moved once while the loss estimate rose from $351.6m to $387.5m.

The rest of the Bitget staged restart, all at 08:00 UTC: ETH on the 29th, USDT on the 30th, other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October. Each stage is a fresh chance for a queue to build; USDT on the 30th is the one that would matter to stablecoin pricing if it does.

Anza's feature-activation window for Solana reopens, but no Alpenglow mainnet date has been announced. Traders who bought the 28 September expectation now have a catalyst without a date, on the thinnest book of the three after a +7.4% week.

A dense quarter-end print: US PCE, ADP employment, the final Q2 GDP estimate, plus Chinese PMIs and German CPI. With October hike odds already near 73%, a firm PCE is the most direct scheduled pressure on the bond market that has been capping this range.
ISM Manufacturing PMI, Challenger layoffs and weekly jobless claims - the read-through into Friday's payrolls.
September employment report (08:30 ET), and the same day Hester Peirce's last day at the SEC. First-Friday payrolls into a Fed that markets already expect to hike on 28 October.

US-Iran technical contacts on the phased Hormuz reopening, against Tehran's seven-day timeline. Progress is the cleanest route to lower oil and lower yields; a collapse puts the 10-year back toward its 5.20% June-2007 high and BTC back toward $83,163.

FOMC rate decision (2:00 p.m. ET, meeting 27-28 October). Market-implied probability of a 25bp hike is roughly 64-73% depending on venue; the US-China trade truce extension announced by Treasury Secretary Bessent runs to 10 January, so tariffs are off the near-term worry list.
